speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing a limp and localized pain, but you do not have a fever or feel acutely distressed. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me exactly where on your body the pain is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the pain is in the left knee, yet you mention he favors that leg. In a 7-year-old boy with these symptoms and no trauma, the pain often originates from the hip rather than the knee itself. Can you tell me if he experiences pain when you press on the front of his hip or when you rotate his leg while he is lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calve-Perthes Disease (Avascular Necrosis of the Femoral Head).

The presentation of a limp and knee pain in a 7-year-old boy, combined with the clinical suspicion of hip pathology despite knee complaints, is highly characteristic of this condition. Given the absence of fever and trauma, this is the leading diagnosis.
